paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved +0.17% on average, with FTSE 100 strongest (+1.08%) and Nasdaq weakest (-0.41%). Brent crude changed +0.13% to 106.2. Gold changed +1.52% to 4,170.5. Bitcoin changed +0.55% to 82,013.3125. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.089%, a relative move of -1.95%. Among the firms tracked, Lazard (+4.02%) and BlackRock (+3.25%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Credit Suisse bankers denied bonuses stripped after UBS takeover (FT World). Switzerland’s top court sides with government decision, overturning ruling of lower court Deals and capital markets: India approves biggest foreign takeover of domestic bank (FT Companies). Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings to buy nearly 61% of IDBI Bank for $5.6bn Central banks and macro: US inflation jumps to 3.7% as Iran war drives up prices (FT World). Rebound in fuel costs has piled pressure on voters ahead of midterm elections Central banks and macro: Rising inflation piles pressure on US voters ahead of midterm elections (FT World). Also in today’s newsletter, are Democrats developing an advantage among independent voters? Geopolitics and trade: How will Big Oil spend its $32bn Iran war windfall? (FT Markets). Investors are keen to see how world’s largest crude companies plan to deploy extra cash generated by soaring energy prices
